source.title: Can Representation Learning Decouple from Loss Minimization? Polar Updates Have an Answer

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies full-batch exact polar updates and representation alignment during loss plateaus. It does not test the listed claims about classification error, spurious minima, depth and shortcuts, initialization, stability-threshold learning rates, or batch normalization.
record.gate_note: The paper reports training-loss plateaus under polar updates, but these are regression or synthetic teacher-student settings and do not report training classification error. The cited edge-of-stability and catapult results are prior work, not this paper’s results.
record.test_reason: The study measures regression-loss cycles and representation alignment under normalized or exact-polar updates. It does not test any stated version. Its discussion of catapults and edge-of-stability gradient descent cites prior results; its own experiments do not measure recovery relative to the initial linearized stability threshold or sharpness hovering at that threshold.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: under stated toy, mean-field and finite-network conditions, polar updates permit representation learning during a loss plateau. The authors restrict the empirical scope and leave applicability to practical Muon training at scale open.
record.recipe_differences: Uses full-batch exact polar or normalized-gradient updates on synthetic regression and teacher-student tasks; the claim versions concern classification-error outcomes and other specified training recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: In deep students, freezing downstream layers, downstream-layer step size, momentum, and orthogonaliser choice change whether a flat loss with continued alignment appears.

fits_no_version.finding: Normalized-gradient and matrix-polar updates approach nonzero regression-loss cycles on objectives where stable plain GD reaches nearly zero loss.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fixed-length normalized updates can create optimizer-dependent regression-loss floors even when a zero-loss solution exists.

fits_no_version.finding: AGOP alignment can improve during sustained flat or rising cycle-mean regression loss in one-hidden-layer students and selected deep residual students with frozen downstream layers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under specified exact-polar training conditions, representation alignment can improve while training loss plateaus.

record.problems: The relevant reported outcomes are regression losses and AGOP alignment, not classification error. Some results are conditional theorems or selected synthetic settings; the paper itself notes that finite-sample illustrations do not verify all theorem hypotheses and that key empirical drift hypotheses remain unverified.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for the paper’s 33 one-hidden-layer configurations, deep depth arms, or freezing-switch conditions were extracted; their reported outcomes concern regression loss and alignment, and the compact rows retain the main distinct settings relevant to the claim’s broad concern about stalled training.

untested.parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 under SGD or Adam, including random labels and size, stopping or regularization comparisons.
Spurious-local-minimum frequencies under gradient descent and their reduction from one or two extra student neurons.
Depth-dependent training-error degradation in plain batch-normalized convolutional networks and its prevention by identity shortcuts; the specified alternative initialization recipes.
Activation-matched initialization comparisons, signal and gradient preservation, and orthogonal-versus-Gaussian effects on training speed or trainable depth.
Recovery or divergence relative to the initial linearized stability limit, curvature reduction during catapults, and full-batch sharpness approaching and hovering at the stability threshold.
Batch-normalization effects on accuracy gain, training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparisons with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: Training-loss oscillations described as near the edge of stability do not by themselves test V5. The plain-network freezing arms measure the loss/alignment separation, not V3's classification-error degradation with depth. No verdict labels are warranted.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 classification, corrupted or random labels, SGD or Adam, and model size or training duration effects.
Spurious local minima frequency under gradient descent as teacher and student widths grow, and the effect of extra student neurons.
Plain versus residual batch-normalized classification networks across depth, and the stated initialization or normalization comparisons.
Activation-matched initialization, signal or gradient propagation, and orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization effects on training speed or depth.
Gradient-descent stability thresholds, catapult recovery, sharpness dynamics, and divergence under the stated learning-rate conditions.
Batch normalization comparisons for speed, accuracy, or learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

rows.subject: M2 (NGD)
rows.operation_detail: Normalized gradient descent on linear regression; the paper reports that runs stop at nonzero loss floors.
rows.value: NGD stops at floors within 0–4% of µ1 η 2 /4.
rows.note: This is a regression loss under normalized updates, not classification error or one of the listed benchmark recipes.
rows.check: Figure 8 supports the reported loss floors and GD baseline. These linear-regression normalized-gradient results measure none of V1–V6.

rows.subject: M3 (matrix Muon)
rows.operation_detail: Matrix Muon on multi-output regression; runs stop at nonzero loss floors.
rows.value: Matrix Muon stops at 1.05–1.39 × λD η 2 r/4.
rows.note: The reported metric is regression loss; the text attributes the ratio to sampling and asymmetric-cycle excess.
rows.check: Figure 8 supports the reported floor ratios and GD baseline. Its caption does not specify the Muon step size, so η = 0.3 is not verified for this comparison. Matrix-regression polar cycles measure none of V1–V6.

rows.subject: 1-HL ReLU student (M4)
rows.operation_detail: Full-batch matrix Muon on teacher-student regression; the paper reports a nearly flat or rising cycle-mean loss while AGOP alignment grows.
rows.measure: Cycle-mean training loss and AGOP alignment
rows.value: Across the 33 configurations, cos2min still rises in 29 over the second half; it has settled by the midpoint in the other four. In three ReLU configurations with rt ≥ 16 it rises but ends below 0.2. Figure 2 reports one ReLU, SiLU and GELU configuration; Figure 3 reports 15 configurations.
rows.uncertainty: Medians over 53 seeds; shaded interquartile ranges.
rows.note: The reported task is teacher-student regression; no classification error is reported. Configuration-level loss and alignment outcomes are not reconstructed into separate rows here.
rows.check: The row combines different subjects and conditions. The 33-configuration outcomes use five seeds per configuration, not 53, and include ReLU, GELU and SiLU teachers with varying ranks, widths and rates. Figure 2's ReLU example has rs = 30, not 50; Figures 2–3 use 53 seeds. Table 2 reports 29 configurations with late gains, but the other four are not all aligned: ReLU rt = 4 ends at 0.670 with a negative late change. These alignment and regression-loss measures bear on no version.

rows.subject: Deep residual ReLU student
rows.operation_detail: Freeze every layer after W1 while W1 trains with full-batch exact polar steps; the cycle-mean loss stays nearly flat as input-AGOP alignment rises.
rows.measure: Cycle-mean training loss and cos2min alignment
rows.value: Across depths 4, 8, 16 and 24, cycle-mean loss stays within 5% in almost all runs while cos2min rises by 0.38–0.53 over the window.
rows.note: These are synthetic Gaussian teacher-student regression experiments, not classification benchmarks.
rows.check: The stated subject and run count describe depth 8, while the value pools depths 4, 8, 16 and 24. Depths 4 and 24 use 24 runs per arm in Appendix F.1; the depth-8 and depth-16 freezing results use 48 runs per arm in Appendix E.2. Add Appendix F.1 to the locator and split these conditions. No plain-versus-residual depth-degradation test corresponding to V3 is reported.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
